# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to either create a new record or modify an existing record in the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. This includes different approaches for single record additions and updates, in addition to the potential for mass upload. During the execution of this process, a user may determine a master data update is required in order to complete an addition or modification. This SOP advises of the necessary steps to take should this be the case.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to the below audience:

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Middle Office

- Embedded Finance (local, hub)

- Alexion Regional Controllership

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

# PROCEDURE

## Process Maps

• Initiate the process when a new lease accounting record or lease accounting record modification is required.

• Determine whether the lease is considered complex, and if yes, raise an AFN query with GFR.

• Assess whether a mass upload is requested, and if yes, route to the GFS Global Lease Team for review.

• Review the request and determine if a mass upload request is accepted by the GFS Global Lease Team.

• Execute mass lease additions or modifications if the mass upload request is accepted.

• Enter lease accounting details if the lease is not complex or mass upload is not requested.

• Determine if additional cost allocation data is required, and if yes, request cost allocation data update.

• Submit the lease accounting record for approval if no additional cost allocation is required.

• Check if errors exist in the submitted record, and if yes, send back for review and correction.

• Update lease accounting master data once the record is approved and error-free.

## Assumptions and Pre-requisites

The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process to which this operating procedure relates:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Assumption / Pre-requisite | Description |
| Pre-requisite | A contract to enter a lease and a purchase order for that lease must exist in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. |
| Pre-requisite | All participants in this process must have the necessary access rights and training required to operate CoStar Real Estate Manager. |
| Pre-requisite | Disposed leases in previous period to be archived by GFS Global Lease Team (refer Appendix). |
| Assumption | All participants must be familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically 'Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)'. |
| Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. |
| Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. |

## Frequency

This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken as additions or modifications are made to leased assets held by AstraZeneca or Alexion entities.

<td colspan="5"><p>Note for Alexion:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Real estate: Global Real Estate (GRE) / CBRE will create/modify the CoStar data for all leases except for accounting schedule. AZ Global Lease Team will proceed with creation/modification of leases accounting schedule.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>Note for CBRE is a global third-party vendor providing commercial real estate and facilities management services and manages Alexion’s global real estate portfolio.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Vehicle lease: Local Finance Markets to update data directly in CoStar (same as AstraZeneca).</p></li>
<li><p>Equipment lease (only applicable for BP70): Regional Controllership team to update data directly in CoStar.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>The intent of this step is to capture all the data required to carry out IFRS 16 compliant accounting within the CoStar system.</p>
<p>There may be a requirement to either create a new lease accounting record or modify an existing record (e.g. renewal, termination, impairment, or general modification). The details are given below:</p>
<p>Commence this process if:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>New lease accounting record is required, or a</p></li>
<li><p>Lease accounting record modification is required</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Check if lease require Accounting Issue Note (AIN) to be raised - An accounting issue with a financial impact of greater than USD 10 million (income statement or balance sheet) should be communicated to GFR. Generally, only unusual, complex or judgemental issues, and issues with a profit impact of greater than USD 20 million, will require a full AIN.</p>
<p>If <strong>yes</strong>, an AIN query should be raised with GFR according to their standard process. Below is the path for AIN template and process</p>
<p><a href="https://azcollaboration.sharepoint.com/:w:/r/sites/AZ150/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7B744AA635-A001-4F2E-BDDE-783C21DFBBD0%7D&amp;file=AIN%20Template%20-%20Material%20new%20lease%20agreement_Final.docx&amp;action=default&amp;mobileredirect=true">Link</a></p>
<p>If <strong>no</strong>, the preparer should continue through the process to determine how the data should be entered in CoStar.</p>
<p>Check if lease is short term (less than 12 months) or low value (below USD 5,000)?<br />
<br />
If <strong>yes</strong>, this is out of IFRS16 scope for AstraZeneca leases and Alexion Vehicle and Other Equipment leases, this should not be entered in CoStar and directly expensed instead.</p>
<p>If <strong>yes</strong>, this is out of IFRS16 scope for Alexion Property leases, the preparer should mark as “Not Applicable” in the lease accounting workflow on the Accounting page in CoStar.</p>
<p>If <strong>no</strong>, the preparer should continue through the process to determine how the data should be entered in CoStar.</p>
<p>Determine if a mass upload should be requested.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The ability to mass upload creations or modifications is retained solely by the GFS Global Lease team. Preparers are able to request mass upload support in the event that:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Over 30 lease records need to be created or modified: or</p></li>
<li><p>Where an entity has over 300 active lease records in a particular asset class (property, Party vehicles or other); or</p></li>
<li><p>3rd party vehicle lease data sent directly to KL team as it falls within mass upload</p></li>
</ul>
<p>If <strong>Yes</strong>, a mass upload request is required:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Refer to step: <strong>8.3.3.11.4 GFS Global Lease Team review the request</strong></p></li>
</ul>
<p>If a mass upload request is accepted by the GFS Global Lease Team:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Refer to process <strong>8.3.3.15</strong> <strong>Execute mass lease additions or modifications</strong> for guidance on the procedure that follows.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> Although mass upload support is possible based on certain criteria being met, it should only be requested as a last resort. The most efficient process, even for large volumes of creations and modifications remains the direct entry method, utilising the productivity features of CoStar. For example, the ability to copy a record.</p>
<p>If <strong>No</strong>, a mass upload is not requested, follow the steps given below to create a new lease accounting record, or modify an existing one:</p>
<p><strong><u>A) Real Estate Assets: Creation</u></strong></p>
<p>The following section will discuss activities for day-to-day lease management.</p>
<p>A.1 Add a Building</p>
<blockquote>
<p>1. Navigate to the Portfolio module. Under the Portfolio module, navigate the list pages by selecting Buildings.</p>
<p><img src="media/image2.png" style="width:4.21399in;height:2.19237in" /></p>
</blockquote>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>Select the ‘+Add’ button to the right of the page and select ‘Building’</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image3.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.34931in" /></p>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Fill the appropriate fields as per lease record requirements and click on ‘Launch’</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Country - Selected as required country</p>
<p>State is a required fields for US and Canada only</p>
<p>Building Name - Company code Lease reference</p>
<p>Portfolio - AstraZeneca/ Alexion</p>
<p>Building Address</p>
<p>Template - Building</p>
<p>Sub-Group should be as per region.</p>
<p><img src="media/image4.png" style="width:3.77083in;height:4.64583in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>It will navigate the user to the new building record where they can complete additional information for that building such as rentable area and building type. Click Save.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image5.png" style="width:6.76864in;height:2.47847in" /></p>
<p>A.2 Add a Lease</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Add’ button to the right of the page in the Leases section of the created Building.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image6.png" style="width:5.91572in;height:0.9244in" /></p>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>Complete the required fields as follows.</p></li>
</ol>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>Building - This is auto populated</p></li>
<li><p>Tenant Legal Name – Company Code</p></li>
<li><p>Lease Type - Select the position for the lease contract. A lessor recognises lease payments from operating leases as income whereas a lessee recognises the right-of-use of the underlying leased asset and a lease liability representing its obligation to make lease payments.</p></li>
<li><p>Lease Template - Since the lease is created at the building record page, it will auto populate as a real estate lease.</p></li>
<li><p>Begin Date – Lease Commencement Date as per contract</p></li>
<li><p>End Date – Lease Expiration Date as per contract</p></li>
<li><p>Accounting Type - Select AP if the lease type includes ‘Lessee’ or ‘Sublessee’, select AR if lease type includes ‘Lessor’ or ‘Sublessor’</p></li>
<li><p>Parent Lease – Leave blank/not relevant for direct entry. Used in ETL.</p></li>
<li><p>Currency type - Select currency used on the lease contract</p></li>
<li><p>Units of Measure – Enter unit of measure if included on contract else allow CoStar to default</p></li>
</ol>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Click ‘Launch’. This will navigate to the new lease record abstract to fill additional information for the leased asset</p></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><p>AstraZeneca Lease Hierarchy - Should be Region&gt;Subregion&gt;Country</p></li>
<li><p>Alexion Lease Hierarchy – Should be Region &gt; Subregion &gt; Country &gt; Company Code &amp; Name</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image7.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:4.0625in" /></p>
<p>The ERP field denotes whether or not the lease belongs an entity that has cutover to SAP S/4HANA (documented as ‘S4’) as part of the current staged entity rollouts to S/4 HANA, replacing the ‘old’ journal entry processing via Blackline. The field is automatically populated based on the Company Code on the Allocations page and ensures that the relevant lease is directed to the appropriate SAP S/4HANA or ECC (Blackline) journal entry export processing.</p>
<p>Click on save button on the abstract. Now there are some areas that need to be completed under the Lease Information section.</p>
<p>A.3 <strong>Lease allocation</strong> which drives the journal coding for lease entries.</p>
<p>Enter Financial Information (Allocations)</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Allocations’ in the left of the lease reference.</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Add Allocation’</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image8.png" style="width:6.38542in;height:1.125in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>Each segment value (See parameters mentioned below) must be populated to save allocation data. Select the blank area underneath any segment and a pencil icon will appear for the user to select.</p></li>
<li><p>Fill parameters to save the allocation and click on ‘Save’.</p>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>The AstraZeneca (ECC) parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre, Product Brand and Internal Order (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment).</p></li>
<li><p>The AstraZeneca (SAP S/4HANA) parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre or WBS (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment), Product Brand. Note: Internal Orders should no longer be used for SAP S/4HANA markets.</p></li>
<li><p>The Alexion parameters include Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre, Payment Company Code and Cost Percent.</p></li>
</ol></li>
</ol>
<p><u>AstraZeneca Allocations<br />
</u><br />
<img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.23732in;height:3.50235in" /></p>
<p><u>Alexion Allocations:<br />
</u></p>
<p><img src="media/image10.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.69028in" /></p>
<blockquote>
<p><strong>Note</strong> 1: Enter the cost percent of the allocation segments. For the majority of the lease population, this will be 100% as the lease is allocated to a single location, activity and banner. If a lease is allocated to several activities, the user will need to continue to add allocation values until the cost percent is equal to 100%.</p>
<p><strong>Note 2</strong>: The Payment Company Code should be the same as the Accounting Company Code in the majority of leases in Alexion. Payment Company Code will be used for tracking appropriate company code for payment files processed by the CBRE (lease administration) team. The Accounting Company Code is the company code value that pulls into the AJD file to post in Blackline.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>A.4 Enter Expenses (To add instalment and base rent)</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Expenses’ in the left menu.</p></li>
</ol>
<blockquote>
<p><img src="media/image11.png" style="width:6.6625in;height:1.06458in" /></p>
</blockquote>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>To add expenses, select ‘+Add’ or in the top menu bar. Quick add is best used for charges that are one-time or do not increase in amount.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image12.png" style="width:6.56181in;height:1.94161in" /></p>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Under Quick Add Charges, complete the Charge Detail section using the following inputs:</p></li>
</ol>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>To enter an amount, first select in the Enter by section either the Fixed or Rate radio button.</p></li>
<li><p>Enter an amount or rate depending on whether fixed or rate was selected in the previous step in the Amount section.</p></li>
<li><p>Area - represents the area amount associated with the charge (e.g. square footage or square meters). This will auto populate based on the rentable area populated on the Details tab.</p></li>
<li><p>Payment Frequency - select frequency per the lease contract. Currency is also determined in this section by selecting from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.</p></li>
<li><p>Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.</p></li>
<li><p>End Date - Defaulted to the Lease Expiration Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.</p></li>
<li><p>Check the Estimated, Taxable, or Prorated checkboxes if the following conditions apply:</p></li>
</ol>
<blockquote>
<p>i. Estimated - Payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.</p>
<p>ii. Taxable - Used for rent charges that will be taxed based on tax authorities entered for the lease. Follow the steps under ‘Generate Tax Charges’.</p>
<p>iii. Prorated - Used to create partial payments for initial or final payment.</p>
<p>When account category is selected Charge Name is auto populated, If this is an initial expense, it should be reflected as original term else name should be changed in the case of a modification<del>.</del></p>
<p><img src="media/image13.png" style="width:5.5in;height:1.52083in" /></p>
</blockquote>
<p>a. Select the vendor ‘**Filler RE Vendor’ from the dropdown. This is the only vendor that is used in the AstraZeneca portfolio. For the Alexion portfolio the vendor can be selected from the dropdown. If the vendor does not exist, it must be added via the CoStar Company record.</p>
<p>b. Check the Estimated checkbox if the payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.</p>
<p>c. Enter a Start Amount in the Charge Generation section.</p>
<p>d. Specify all other details, such as:</p>
<blockquote>
<p>i. Payment Frequency - Select frequency per the lease contract.</p>
<p>ii. Currency - Select from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.</p>
<p>iii. Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.</p>
</blockquote>
<p><img src="media/image14.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:2.59792in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>Click ‘Generate’ to generate the charge.</p></li>
<li><p>Review charges in the expenses schedule to confirm accuracy. Add additional charges as needed.</p></li>
<li><p>This is how a lease expense schedule is prepared</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image15.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.13542in" /></p>
<p><strong><u>A5) Create an accounting schedule</u></strong></p>
<p>Follow the steps below to create an accounting schedule.</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Click on accounting navigation at the left side</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image16.png" style="width:7.01667in;height:3.47153in" /></p>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>In the top right, select Add to create a new accounting schedule.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule and Click Calculate Values.<br />
<strong>Note:</strong> some fields will be derived from data in the abstract and will not need to be selected here.</p>
<p>Classification - Select IFRS16 from the dropdown data</p>
<p>Amortization Profile - Select IFRS16 from the dropdown data</p>
<p>Journal Entry Profile - Based on asset type - Select IFRS16 - Property from the dropdown data (Please note, there are separate Journal Entry Profiles starting with ‘S4’ to be used for all leases that should be exported via the SAP S/4HANA ledger)</p>
<p>Accounting Term Begin - Select Current Commencement Date from the dropdown data</p>
<p>Accounting Term End - Select Current Expiration Date from the dropdown data</p>
<p>Discount Rate Profile - System will suggest a best match discount rate</p>
<p>Payment Timing - Can be changed from the Annual Rate dropdown</p>
<p><img src="media/image17.png" style="width:7.01667in;height:2.97778in" /></p>
<p>Note: Journal Entry Profile available for use are as below. Selection should be based on asset type and nature of accounting event. Please ensure you select the correct profile based on whether the relevant lease has been cutover to SAP S/4HANA or not. If the lease should be directed to the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry export process, please only select journal entry profiles starting with ‘S4’. Continue to use all other journal entry profiles (i.e., not starting with ‘S4’) for all other leases. Other than the dropdown data below should not be in use.</p>
<p><img src="media/image18.png" style="width:2.52083in;height:3.35417in" /></p>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Once clicked on Calculate Values, Save and Close.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image19.png" style="width:7.01667in;height:3.47153in" /></p>
<p>Follow the steps below to <strong>modify lease accounting record for Real Estate Assets</strong>:</p>
<p><strong><u>B) Real Estate Assets: Modification</u></strong></p>
<p>B.1 Modify Expenses / Expense Accounts</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>To modify charges, navigate to the Expense page on the lease record.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the ellipsis on the relevant charge followed by ‘Edit’.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image20.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.23333in" /></p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Make necessary modifications to the amount, account, notes or other detail associated with the charge.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image21.png" style="width:6.87587in;height:2.70583in" /></p>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Click ‘Apply’, followed by ‘Save and close’.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Note: To add a charge, click Quick Add and fill the charge details accordingly. There should be no overlapping dates. To delete a charge, select the ellipsis icon to the right of the given charge line followed by ‘Delete’</p>
<p>B.2 Review Payment Dates</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Navigate to the expenses page on the lease record.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Under the Actions menu select the ellipsis on the right-hand side, followed by ‘Edit’.</p>
<blockquote>
<p><img src="media/image22.png" style="width:6.68279in;height:0.85127in" /></p>
</blockquote>
<p><img src="media/image23.png" style="width:6.33945in;height:1.79586in" /></p>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>Review the pay on dates to ensure accuracy.</p></li>
<li><p>If necessary, modify the proration/first recurring payment date by editing the charge.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.</p>
<p>B.3 Enter Lease Option</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Navigate to the lease record on the RE Abstract and select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.</p></li>
<li><p>Navigate to the Lease Options section of the abstract.</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Add’.</p></li>
<li><p>Enter all of the relevant option information including Option Type, Option Status, Description, Start date and End date in the Lease Option section.</p></li>
</ol>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>Option Status – Should be set to Active, Declined or Exercised.</p></li>
</ol>
<ol start="5" type="1">
<li><p>If the contract lists specific rents or charges associated with that option, enter the information in the Option Charge Generation section. (See Enter Expenses section for help with inputs).</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Save and Close’.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.</p>
<p>B.4 Execute Lease Option</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Navigate to the lease record and select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner.</p></li>
<li><p>Navigate to the Lease Options section of the abstract.</p></li>
<li><p>Click the edit icon next to the option you would like to exercise.</p></li>
<li><p>Next to Option Status, click ‘Save and Exercise’.</p></li>
<li><p>Complete the fields in the exercise option wizard including updating lease dates, adding relevant supporting documentation such as an amendment, and reviewing the updated lease information.</p></li>
<li><p>Review the lease abstract to ensure the correct dates are reflected.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> this feature is not applicable to the AstraZeneca portfolio as CoStar does not process payments.</p>
<p><strong><u>C) Equipment Assets: Creation</u></strong></p>
<p>The following section will discuss activities for day-to-day lease administration of non-real estate assets.</p>
<p>C.1 Add an Equipment Lease</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Navigate to the Portfolio module.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the ‘Add’ button to the right of the page and click ‘Equipment Lease’</p></li>
<li><p>Complete the required fields including</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Portfolio – AstraZeneca / Alexion</p>
<p>Supplier - According to company code and asset type</p>
<p>Legal Entity - Company Code</p>
<p>Template - Equipment Lease</p>
<p>Begin and end date</p>
<p>Currency type</p>
<p><img src="media/image24.png" style="width:7.01667in;height:2.79097in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>Click ‘Launch’. This will navigate you to the new lease record where you can complete additional information (Client Lease ID - Lease reference, Address, Organizational hierarchy, Ownership type) to the leased asset.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image25.png" style="width:7.01667in;height:2.59028in" /></p>
<p>The ERP field denotes whether or not the lease belongs an entity that has cutover to SAP S/4HANA (documented as ‘S4’) as part of the current staged entity rollouts to S/4 HANA, replacing the ‘old’ journal entry processing via Blackline. The field is automatically populated based on the Company Code on the Allocations page and ensures that the relevant lease is directed to the appropriate SAP S/4HANA or ECC (Blackline) journal entry export processing.</p>
<p>C.2 <strong>Lease Allocation</strong> which drives the journal coding for lease entries.</p>
<p>Enter Financial Information (Allocations)</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Allocations’ in the left of the lease reference</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Edit’ in the top right corner</p></li>
<li><p>Select ‘Add Allocation’</p></li>
<li><p>Each segment value must be populated to save allocation data. Select the blank area underneath any segment and a pencil icon will appear for the user to select</p></li>
<li><p>Fill all 4 parameters to save the allocation. The number of parameters to complete depend on whether the Equipment Lease is in the AstraZeneca or Alexion portfolio. The AstraZeneca parameters include Company Code, Cost Centre and/or Internal Order/WBS (Internal Order to be removed after all entities are leveraging the new integration to SAP S/4HANA), Product Brand and Cost Percent. The Alexion parameters include Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre, Payment Company Code and Cost Percent.</p></li>
<li><p>Click on Save.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image8.png" style="width:6.38542in;height:1.125in" /></p>
<p>AstraZeneca Allocations:</p>
<p><img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.56553in;height:3.68665in" /></p>
<p>Alexion Allocations:</p>
<p><img src="media/image10.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.69028in" /></p>
<blockquote>
<p>Note: 1. Enter the cost percent of the allocation segments. For the majority of the lease population, this will be 100% as the lease is allocated to a single location, activity and banner. If a lease is allocated to several activities, the user will need to continue to add allocation values until the cost percent is equal to 100%.</p>
<p><strong>Note 2</strong>: The Payment Company Code should be the same as the Accounting Company Code in the majority of leases in Alexion. Payment Company Code will be used for tracking appropriate company code for payment files processed by the CBRE (lease administration) team. The Accounting Company Code is the company code value that pulls into the AJD file to post in Blackline.</p>
</blockquote>
<p>C.3 <strong>Enter Expenses</strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>To add expenses, select ‘+Add’ in the top menu bar, followed by ‘Add Charges’.</p></li>
<li><p>Under Quick Add: Add Charges, complete the Create Charges section detail.</p></li>
<li><p>When account category is selected, ‘Charge Name’ is auto populated. If this is an initial expense, it should be reflecting as original term, else name should be changed in the case of a modification<del>.</del></p></li>
<li><p>Select the vendor ‘**Filler RE Vendor’ from the dropdown. This is the only vendor that is used in the AstraZeneca portfolio.</p></li>
<li><p>Check the Estimated checkbox if the payment is an estimated amount and should not appear in AP processing reports.</p></li>
<li><p>Enter a Start Amount in the Charge Generation section.<br />
Specify all other details, such as:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Payment Frequency - Select frequency per the lease contract.</p></li>
<li><p>Currency - Select from the dropdown menu; this is a dynamic search box where you can type out the three-character currency code such as USD.</p></li>
<li><p>Start Date - Defaulted to the Lease Commencement Date from the lease abstract. Modify if necessary.</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<ol start="7" type="1">
<li><p>Click ‘’Generate’ to generate the charge.</p></li>
<li><p>Review charges in the expenses schedule to confirm accuracy. Add additional charges as needed.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>D) <strong><u>Equipment Assets: Modification</u></strong></p>
<p>D.1 Modify Expenses</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>To modify charges, navigate to the Expense page on the lease record.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the ellipsis icon next to the charge you need to modify. Select Edit.</p></li>
<li><p>Make necessary modifications to the amount, account, notes or other detail associated with the charge.</p></li>
<li><p>Click ‘Save’.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>Note: To delete a charge, select the ellipsis icon to the right of the given charge line, followed by ‘Delete’.</p>
<p>E) <strong><u>Remeasuring an Accounting Schedule</u></strong></p>
<p>A remeasurement event occurs due to any change to the lease agreement that requires a revaluation of the right-of-use asset. Examples include a lease renewal (extension), lease termination or modification of fixed charges.</p>
<p>1) In the Accounting Summary section of the Accounting page of a lease, select the ellipsis icon next to the schedule you wish to remeasure. A pop-up menu is displayed showing the available types of remeasurement.</p>
<p>2) Select the appropriate listed remeasurement.</p>
<p>3) Should the remeasurement effective date impact an exported period, there would be a need for intervention from the Global Lease Accounting team to perform unexport/unapproved prior to remeasurement of the schedule. Refer to <strong>Appendix - IFRS16 Guide on Global Lease Accounting Team Intervention in CoStar (by scenario)</strong></p>
<p>E.1 Renewal/Data Correction</p>
<ul>
<li><p>A lease renewal is an extension on an expiring lease. During the renewal process, the lessor and lessee negotiate new lease terms or remove old ones. The new commencement and expiration dates must be re-defined for the amortization schedule to recalculate and revalue the asset appropriately.</p></li>
<li><p>Data Correction is performed when there is data correction made in the expense pertaining dates and amount</p></li>
<li><p>If the schedule has a workflow status of Reviewed prior to the rent schedule being modified, the status will automatically change to Open for Preparation. Once the expense is triggered.</p></li>
<li><p>The following are true when performing a renewal action on an existing schedule:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>The new date range must begin after the first period. If the new range is before an approved period, the system will calculate a retroactive adjustment.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event, such as a renewal, that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ul></li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p>accounting schedule and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.</p>
</blockquote>
<ul>
<li><p>The system will automatically calculate the difference in the newly calculated Present Value and the end liability balance prior to the new date range as the liability adjustment.</p></li>
<li><p>The Asset Adjustment will default to an amount equal to the liability adjustment; however, you can still edit the Total Asset Adjustment by updating the manual adjustment field if further modifications are needed, such as adjusting for an impaired asset. Simply input the manual asset adjustment field with the desired value before saving the amortization schedule.</p></li>
</ul>
<ul>
<li><p>Before performing a renewal, the user must add new or extend existing fixed charges on the Expense or Revenue page of the lease.</p></li>
</ul>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Renewal’.</p></li>
<li><p>Complete the required fields as appropriate including:</p></li>
</ol>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>Accounting Term Begin - Date of the execution letter/date the renewal was exercised</p></li>
<li><p>Accounting Term End - The new lease expiration date according to the terms of the renewal.</p></li>
</ol>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Click’ Calculate Values’</p></li>
<li><p>Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as the present value, adjustment amounts, or implicit rates. The amortization periods prior to the new accounting begin date will be preserved. The level expense will adjust beginning on the new accounting begin date. Notice that the adjustment amount will automatically populate with the balance from the prior period.</p></li>
<li><p>Click ‘Save &amp; Close’.</p></li>
<li><p>Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image26.png" style="width:6.89583in;height:3.58333in" /></p>
<p>E.2 Impairment</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Impairment is a permanent decline in the value of an asset. This situation exists when the cash flows or other benefits generated by an asset decline, as determined through a periodic assessment. For example, the lease administrator may discover that the fair value of an asset is far less than the carrying amount. Therefore, the difference between the fair value of the asset and it carrying amount would be written off. The payment terms do not change in the case of an impairment and thus the lease liability amortization remains intact.</p></li>
<li><p>Impairments can be prospective or retroactive, depending on the impairment.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>A retroactive adjustment is an adjustment to an amortization schedule based on an event that has already occurred but was not recorded at the time of occurrence. In this case the application will adjust prior periods of the accounting schedule, and the adjusting entries will be sent in the upcoming period.</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ul>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Impairment’. The Remeasure – Impairment page is displayed.</p></li>
<li><p>Complete the following required fields as appropriate:</p></li>
</ol>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>Accounting Term Begin - Date of the impairment.</p></li>
<li><p>Accounting Term End - The same Period to date as the original expiration date.</p></li>
</ol>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Enter a number into the Manual Asset Adjustment field. As an impairment reflects a drop in value, this should be a negative number.</p></li>
<li><p>Click ‘Calculate Values’.</p></li>
<li><p>Verify that the system has finished calculating all numbers such as present value, adjustment amounts or implicit rates.</p></li>
<li><p>Click <strong>‘</strong>Save &amp; Close’.</p></li>
<li><p>Review schedule and update Accounting Workflow status.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image27.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:3.58333in" /></p>
<p>E.3 Termination</p>
<p>When a termination event occurs, the amortization schedule needs to be updated so future payments are removed from the calculation and the remaining balance is capitalized at an accelerated pace.</p>
<p>The new date range typically begins the day you are notified about the termination and ends on the day of the termination. This determines how many periods by which to divide the remaining balance. <strong>Note:</strong> If the termination date falls within an exported period, Preparer should inform the Global Lease Accounting team to perform necessary action to unexport and unapprove the period prior to remeasurement of termination. For an example, assuming it is March 2023 closing, if a termination date falls within Dec 2022, preparer to move the workflow status of the lease to Open for Preparation and, inform the Global Lease Accounting team to unexport and unapprove journals from Dec 2022 to March 2023 Preparer should then be able to remeasure termination.</p>
<p>There are two types of termination where steps are given below:</p>
<p><strong>Termination: Normal Expired</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><p>As this is a termination for a normal expired lease, a remeasurement is sufficient. Click on the ellipsis in Actions - Remeasure – Termination</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image28.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:2.35417in" /></p>
<p>2. Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Accounting Term Begin - Direct Entry date. Same as per Accounting Term End.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile - IFRS16 Vehicle – Disposal (Alternatively, select ‘S4 IFRS 16 -Vehicle Disposal’, or other alternatives based on the relevant asset type for leases that should follow the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry process).</p></li>
<li><p>Discount Rate Profile - Select Direct Entry from the dropdown data</p></li>
<li><p>Annual Rate - By default should remain as 0%, as this will allow the system to calculate the gain/loss portion with the early termination date.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image29.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:3.625in" /></p>
<p>3. Click ‘Calculate Values’, followed by ‘Save and Close’. A termination schedule is created under Accounting Events.</p>
<p><img src="media/image30.png" style="width:6.9375in;height:1.77083in" /></p>
<p><strong>Full Termination: Early Termination</strong></p>
<p>1. As this is an early termination for a lease, a remeasurement is sufficient. Click on the ellipsis in Actions -</p>
<p>Remeasure - Full Termination</p>
<p><img src="media/image31.png" style="width:6.91667in;height:2.47917in" /></p>
<p>2. Select the required data from the dropdown in the details of the schedule:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Accounting Term End: Direct Entry date as Early Termination Date. By default, the Accounting Term Begin will follow the same as the Early Termination Date entered.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile: IFRS16 Vehicle – Disposal (Alternatively, select S4 IFRS 16 -Vehicle Disposal, or other alternatives based on the relevant asset type for leases that should follow the new SAP S/4HANA journal entry process). Discount Rate Profile: By default, it will auto-populate Direct Entry.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image32.png" style="width:6.97917in;height:3.65625in" /></p>
<p>3. Click ‘Calculate Values’, followed by ‘Save and Close’. A full termination schedule is created under Accounting Events.</p>
<p><img src="media/image33.png" style="width:6.97917in;height:1.27083in" /></p>
<p>Check, if an additional cost allocation data is required?</p>
<ul>
<li><p>If Yes, refer to <strong>Task #8.3.3.11.3: 4.7.3 Request cost allocation date update.</strong></p></li>
<li><p>If no, refer to <strong>Task# 8.3.3.11.2: 4.7.2 Submit lease accounting record for approval</strong></p></li>
</ul></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

# RESPONSIBILITIES

## Roles and Teams

The table below provides a summary of the roles and teams relevant to the associated process map:

| **Role / Team Name** | **Description** |
|----|----|
| GFS Global Lease Team | Responsible for the execution of mass upload and allocation data additions and modifications within the lease accounting system. |
| Embedded Finance/GFS Middle Office | Responsible for entering lease accounting data into the system where this activity hasn’t been transitioned to the middle office. |
| Global Real Estate (GRE) / CBRE | Responsible for entering lease accounting data into the system for the Alexion Real Estate leases only. |
| Alexion Regional Controllers | Responsible for entering lease accounting data for Alexion Equipment Leases only. |

# Alexion Specific Process Maps

• Collect regional lease data and update lease data in CoStar system to initiate the process.

• Create lease accounting schedule and submit lease accounting record for approval, moving workflow status from Open for Preparation to Prepared in CoStar.

• Review lease accounting schedule and determine if it has been prepared correctly, with option to return for corrections if needed.

• Conduct second review of the lease accounting schedule after initial approval, moving status from Prepared to Approved in CoStar.

• Review lease accounting schedule again and move from Approved to Reviewed status in CoStar upon confirmation of correctness.

• Approve journal entries for the period in CoStar system.

• Export journal entries for the period from CoStar to BlackLine for reconciliation.

• Perform reconciliation in BlackLine system and process additional accounting adjustments if required.

• Complete automated journal entry posting in BlackLine system to finalise the process.

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the activities required to approve and review a newly created or modified lease record, to ensure the record is accurate, complete and valid from an accounting perspective, before it is included in the period end activity that generates the relevant IFRS 16 general ledger accounting entries. The executor of an approval will depend on a country’s classification in the control environment. The GFS Global Lease team will carry out this activity as a technical step for the majority of entities. However, the largest entities (top 80% liabilities value in USD) will require a local approval.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to the below audience:

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Middle Office

- Embedded Finance (local, hub)

- Alexion Regional Controllership

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion, that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

## Assumptions and Pre-requisites

The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Assumption / Pre-requisite | Description |
| Pre-requisite | A contract to enter into a lease and a purchase order for that lease exists in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. |
| Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. |
| Assumption | All participants are familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically ‘Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)’ |
| Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. |
| Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. |

## Frequency

This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken as additions or modifications are made to AstraZeneca / Alexion entities leased assets.

The table below contains a summary of the system(s) and accesses required for the process this operating procedure relates to:

| Physical System Name | User Profile / Access Type Required | Description |
| CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Lease Accounting – Workflow - Lease Approver | Required to approve a newly created or modified lease record with a status of ‘prepared’ |
| CoStar Real Estate Manager (CoStar) | Lease Accounting – Workflow - Lease Reviewer | Required to review a newly created or modified lease record with a status of ‘approved’ |

<p>Referring the below steps to review accounting schedule (Individual or Batch by lease)</p>
<p><strong>Individual by Lease – Review accounting attributes</strong></p>

<p><img src="media/image15.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:2.20347in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to insert a comment to change the workflow status from Approved to Reviewed.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image16.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:2.41875in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>Click ‘Save’. The workflow status will appear as Reviewed.</p></li>

<p><img src="media/image17.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:2.41667in" /></p>
<p><strong>Batch – Review accounting attributes</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><p>On the Accounting module, in the left navigation menu, click on ‘Batch Change Workflow’.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image4.png" style="width:6.26806in;height:2.91181in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>The top of the page consists of the Lease Filters section, where Reviewer selects the required selections as below:</p>
<ul>

<li><p>Classification: IFRS 16</p></li>
<li><p>Workflow Status: Approved</p></li>

<p><img src="media/image18.png" style="width:6.26806in;height:2.95417in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>Click ‘Apply Filters’. The Leases Filtered Table at the bottom of the page displays the leases as filtered by Reviewer’s selections, and the Lease Filters section collapses.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image19.png" style="width:6.29644in;height:2.4874in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>To review the accounting attributes, Reviewer to extract the roll forward report (steps in 8.3.3.14 – Execute lease accounting reporting). For example, review the following:</p>

<li><p>End Date</p></li>
<li><p>Cost Center / Internal Order</p></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Once accounting attributes are reviewed, Reviewer to select the leases in the Leases Filtered Table for which to change the status. To select all leases, select the check box in header row of the leftmost column.</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image20.png" style="width:6.26806in;height:1.12917in" /></p>
<ul>

<p><img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.49703in;height:2.65184in" /></p>
<ul>

</ul>

<ul>

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to generate a report from CoStar Real Estate Manager. This could be one of the standards, pre-configured reports, or a user created report, depending on the underlying requirement. All users have full access to the CoStar reporting module and are expected to self-serve their own reporting demands.

# AUDIENCE

As all users of CoStar Real Estate Manager have the required access, the distinction this SOP makes is:

- Licensed CoStar Users

- Non-Licensed holders

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

## Frequency

This process can be ad hoc as required or executed regularly as part of a period end close process such as schedule/disclosure submissions and balance sheet reconciliation.

|----|----|----|----|----|
| Manual | CPX015-01 | Review of CoStar Accounting Summary report to confirm unit’s leases are complete and accurate (review includes a check that all leases are at Workflow Approval Status = Approved or Reviewed) – manual control | SOX and FCF | GFS Middle office /Embedded finance |
| Manual | CPX017-02 | FX rates in CoStar \[per Accounting IFRS 16 Disclosures report\] are checked to the AZ Treasury FX Rates SharePoint site – manual control | FCF | GFS Technology - System Delivery R2R |
| Manual | CPX017-03 | Discount factors in CoStar \[per Discount Rate Validation report\] are checked to the Discount Factors provided by AZ Treasury | FCF | GFS Technology - System Delivery R2R |

<td colspan="5"><p>There are common Ad Hoc data sets and Data fields in the reports in CoStar</p>
<p><strong>Common Ad Hoc Data Sets</strong></p>
<p>• Lease Summary – Includes all fields from Center, Store and Lease abstracts</p>
<p>• GL Event Summary – Includes ‘GL’ fields for expense/revenue charge schedule such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes</p>
<p>• GL Exported Transactions – Transaction history log, includes ‘GL’ fields for all exported expense/revenue charges such as Expense Account, Expense Name, Expense Start Date, Expense End Date and Expense Notes</p>
<p>• Lease Accounting by Period with Allocations– Includes accounting schedule inputs and balances by period</p>
<p><strong>Common Ad Hoc Data Fields</strong></p>
<p>Generally, the field names in the ad hoc data sets are aligned with the naming convention of the field on the lease abstract. The following fields are calculated fields in the data sets that are useful for reporting.</p>
<p>• Current Term Remaining – Calculates from today’s date to current lease expiration date</p>
<p>• Current Annual Rent – Calculates annual rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent</p>
<p>• Current Month Expenses – Calculates sum of total monthly rent and non-rent charges</p>
<p>• Current Month Rent Expenses – Calculates sum of monthly rent based on ledger accounts configured as Is Rent</p>
<p>• Remaining Renewal Options – Defines number of renewal options that are Active</p>
<p>• Next Option Date/s – Defines critical dates associated with next available option such as Option Begin Date, Option End Date and Option Notification Start Date</p>
<p>See below steps to execute specific reports with required parameters.</p>
<p>Accounting Roll-Forward Report</p>

#

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to either create new records or modify existing records using the mass processing (ETL) tool in the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. These activities can differ depending on the asset class (property, vehicles or other) but will only ever be executed by the GFS Global Lease Team. This process is considered highly complex and should not be undertaken unless the volume qualifications documented in the AZ Global Lease Accounting Standard are met at a minimum.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Middle Office

- Embedded Finance (local, hub)

- Alexion Regional Controllership

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

## 4.2 Assumptions and Prerequisites

The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Assumption / Prerequisite | Description |
| Pre-requisite | A contract to enter a lease and a purchase order for that lease exists in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. |
| Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. |
| Pre-requisite | A qualifying request exists to trigger the mass upload process. |
| Assumption | All participants are familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically ‘Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)’ |
| Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. |
| Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. |

## Frequency

This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken as additions or modifications are made to an AstraZeneca or Alexion entities leased assets

<td colspan="4"><p>Once a template has been populated with all the desired data, Navigate to the ETL tool.</p>
<p><img src="media/image4.png" style="width:6.62296in;height:3.48333in" /></p>
<p>Select <strong>Import</strong> Data at the top left-hand corner of the screen</p>
<p><img src="media/image5.png" style="width:6.60616in;height:1.80025in" /></p>
<p>This will take the user to the ETL import wizard. Select the <strong>Choose File</strong> button and find the populated template you wish to upload into the application</p>
<p><img src="media/image6.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:0.61736in" /></p>
<p>Once a template is selected, the tool will populate the information about the template so the user can confirm the details of the file that was selected. The user should confirm the File Name is correct, the Portfolio is correct, and the Import Template Name matches the desired ETL type. If the details match expectations, select <strong>Next</strong></p>
<p><img src="media/image7.png" style="width:6.24249in;height:2.87315in" /></p>
<p>The tool will then go through the validation process, confirming if the data in the template is in the appropriate format for upload. During this process, the tool will also tell the end user how many records the application will insert and how many records the application will update.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>A record that is being inserted signifies that there are no other records of this type with a matching key field (Source Import ID). The application will create new records for these line items.</p></li>
<li><p>A record that is being updated signifies that there are records of this type with matching key field (Source Import ID), so the tool will replace all associated data in the application with the data in the template.</p></li>
<li><p>It is the user’s responsibility to confirm these metrics are accurate and that the data should be inserted or updated as this screen suggests</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image7.png" style="width:6.24249in;height:2.87315in" /></p>
<p>As template import the data in ETL, sometimes there is validation error and warning shown. It is due to incorrect fields were selected and showing in Field Name, Row Number and source data table. So, to avoid the error, Select correct field in template and import again with appropriable template until validation get successfully.</p>
<p><img src="media/image8.png" style="width:6.45097in;height:2.998in" /></p>
<p>Once the data has been successfully validated by the application, select the <strong>Continue</strong> button to move on to the final stage of the ETL loading process</p>
<p><img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.26577in;height:3.67688in" /></p>
<p>The application will show for a final time the number of records that will be inserted and updated as well as the number of records that are invalid and will be skipped. If all this information looks correct, select <strong>Process Valid Records</strong> to begin loading the data.</p>
<p><img src="media/image10.png" style="width:6.57654in;height:3.33817in" /></p>
<p>The tool will then take the user back to the Imports screen, where the template that was just validated will be in a Queued status. This means the template is waiting to be uploaded but has not begun loading yet.</p>
<p><img src="media/image11.png" style="width:6.53101in;height:3.45531in" /></p>
<p>The Status will update to In Progress once the template begins loading to the application.</p>
<p>The Status will update to Completed once the template has been successfully loaded into the application. The Records Processed column shows how many records were successfully loaded.</p>
<p><img src="media/image12.png" style="width:6.35065in;height:3.89995in" /></p>
<p>Check if the addition or modification is successfully mass uploaded?</p>
<p>In the case of yes, Move to Step <strong>8.3.3.15.5 4.6.5 Inform in Country requestor</strong> via AZNextgen</p>
<p>In case of No, check if Master data require to update?</p>
<p>If Yes, Move to step <strong>8.3.3.16 Update lease accounting master data.</strong></p>
<p>If No, move back to follow step <strong>8.3.3.15.2. 4.6.2 Consult with In-country finance to confirm template attributes.</strong></p></td>
</tr>

#

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to update the accounting master data lists (cost centres and internal orders) to make new accounting attributes available for selection or update existing accounting attributes, so that they may be selected on lease accounting records. This SOP advises of the necessary steps to take should this be the case.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Middle Office

- Embedded Finance (local, hub)

- Alexion Regional Controllership

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

# PROCEDURE

## Process Map

## Assumptions and Prerequisites

The table below contains a summary of the assumptions and pre-requisites required for the process this operating procedure relates to:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Assumption / Prerequisite | Description |
| Pre-requisite | A contract to enter into a lease and a purchase order for that lease exists in an AstraZeneca purchasing system. |
| Pre-requisite | All participants in this process have the necessary access and training required in CoStar Real Estate Manager. |
| Assumption | All participants are familiar with the AstraZeneca Group Accounting Manual, specifically ‘Section B12 Leases (IFRS 16)’ |
| Assumption | The requirements documented in the AstraZeneca Group Treasury Policy, 11.1 Leasing Policy (right of use assets) have been fulfilled prior to entering into a lease. |
| Assumption | The data and accounting attributes required to create a lease accounting record are known to the preparer of the record. |

## Frequency

This is an ad-hoc process, undertaken to update master data to an AstraZeneca / Alexion entity leased assets.

<td colspan="4"><p>Once the requirement has been updated in documents and shared with the Global lease accounting team to update the master data, follow the below step to execute it.</p>
<p>Under the Admin module, Click on Allocation centers</p>
<p><img src="media/image3.png" style="width:6.58401in;height:3.4748in" /></p>

<p>Select the allocations in the left-hand navigation bar. There are four segments available in the AstraZeneca Portfolio allocations:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>The AstraZeneca (ECC) allocation segments include Company Code, Cost Centre, Internal Order (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment) and Product Brand.</p></li>
<li><p>The AstraZeneca (SAP S/4HANA) allocation segments include Company Code, Cost Centre or WBS (Use the Internal Order/WBS segment) and Product Brand. Note: Internal Order should not be used for SAP S/4HANA markets.</p></li>
<li><p>The Alexion segments include Accounting Company Code, Cost Centre and Payment Company Code.</p></li>

<p><img src="media/image4.png" style="width:6.54114in;height:2.56191in" /></p>

<ul>
<li><p>Centre, Code &amp; Number - Company Code</p></li>
<li><p>Segment - Select Company Code from the dropdown</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image5.png" style="width:5.87364in;height:2.99821in" /></p>
<p>Click on the save button. The newly created Company Code should appear as below.</p>
<p><img src="media/image6.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:1.09306in" /></p>
<p><strong>B).</strong> If a cost center to added, fill the required detail as given below</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Center – Cost Center - CC General Name</p></li>
<li><p>Code - Company Code</p></li>
<li><p>Number - Cost Center</p></li>
<li><p>Segment - Select Cost Center from the dropdown</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image7.png" style="width:4.97936in;height:4.43654in" /></p>
<p><img src="media/image8.png" style="width:3.24104in;height:2.07795in" /></p>
<p>Once saved, the new Cost Centre should appear as below:</p>
<p><img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:1.09375in" /></p>
<p>C). If an Internal Order/WBS needs to be added: fill the below fields as given below</p>
<p>For ECC:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Center – Internal Order - Internal Order Name</p></li>
<li><p>Code - Company Code</p></li>
<li><p>Number - Internal Order</p></li>
<li><p>Segment - Select Internal Order/WBS from the dropdown</p></li>
</ul>
<p>For SAP S/4HANA:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Center – WBS – WBS Name</p></li>
<li><p>Code – Company Code</p></li>
<li><p>Number – WBS</p></li>
<li><p>Segment – Select Internal Order/WBS from the dropdown (Once all entities have cutover to SAP S/4HANA, this segment can be renamed to just WBS)</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image10.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:0.70298in" /></p>
<p><img src="media/image11.png" style="width:5.86327in;height:2.88372in" /></p>
<p>After clicking on the save button, the new Internal Order/WBS should appear as below:</p>
<p><img src="media/image12.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:1.16964in" /></p>
<p>D). If a product brand needs to add, fill the below detail:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Center – Product Brand - Product Brand Name</p></li>
<li><p>Code - Product Brand</p></li>
<li><p>Number - Product Brand</p></li>
<li><p>Segment - Select Product Brand from the dropdown</p></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image13.png" style="width:5.77083in;height:2.54167in" /></p>

<p><img src="media/image14.png" style="width:6.37265in;height:1.13155in" /></p>

<p>Filter the segment field as per the requirement (e.g., CC, Code, Number).</p>
<p><img src="media/image15.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:3.11667in" /></p>
<p>Once segment is filtered, click on the yellow pencil box located at the right side section. Make necessary updates to the segment (e.g., see cost center example above) and then click on the save button. This is how master data is updated and information will be reflected</p>

#

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to explain the standard set of activities required to process lease accounting records and create the necessary outputs required to build journal entries from the CoStar Real Estate Manager system. This includes validating the lease accounting records and exporting the data. In the standard process this data is automatically sent to BlackLine where it is automatically prepared as journal entries before being posted.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to:

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Middle Office

- Embedded Finance (local, hub)

- Alexion Regional Controllership

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

|  |  |
|----|----|
| Business Process | Description |
| Global | This process applies to all leases both for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR |

<td colspan="4"><h3 id="review-lease-alerts-page">Review Lease Alerts page </h3></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="2">Responsible</td>
<td>Accountable</td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td colspan="5" style="text-align: left;"><p>This process starts with <strong>8.3.3.13 Approve and review lease accounting record</strong></p>
<p>In this process, check accounting workflow is filtered by “Prepared” and “Approved” to ensure:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Any new leases created have an accounting schedule added that has been reviewed before processing lease accounting monthly entries</p></li>
<li><p>Any modifications added due to any reason have been reviewed before processing lease accounting monthly entries</p></li>
</ul>
<p>In the Accounting module, select “Lease Alerts” to view the lease alerts by severity or another criterion. This view is overall for the entire portfolio you have access to.</p>
<p><img src="media/image2.png" style="width:6.24211in;height:3.18863in" /></p>
<p>If you have access to both the AstraZeneca and Alexion portfolios, use the Portfolio filter at the top of the page to select the relevant portfolio you would like to filter for.</p>
<p><img src="media/image3.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:1.44861in" /></p>
<p>To view lease alerts by individual lease, at the top right page of the Abstract, Accounting, Expenses, and/or Revenue pages for that lease, an alerts button will display with the number of alerts in parentheses and the text displaying in accordance with the colour of the most severe alert.</p>
<p><img src="media/image4.png" style="width:3.5in;height:1.025in" /></p>
<p>Click the button to display the Lease Alerts pop-up window to process the alerts. After closing out, navigate back to the Lease Alerts page using the breadcrumb trail at the top left of the page.</p></td>
</tr>

<td colspan="7"><p>This step is performed when two validations are completed</p>
<p>In the Accounting module, select ‘Journal Entries to Approve’.</p>
<p>On the Journal Entry Approval screen, select the filters desired to narrow down the search results but all others are optional.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Portfolio – AstraZeneca / Alexion.</p></li>
<li><p>Country - Select country as required.</p></li>
<li><p>Period - Current month when performed.</p></li>
<li><p>Workflow status - All workflow status should be reviewed prior to approving journal entries.</p></li>
<li><p>Classification type: IFRS 16.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile: Use the dropdown to select the relevant profiles, depending on whether the lease you are approving should be directed towards the SAP S/4HANA or ECC(Blackline) journal entry processing. For all leases that have cutover to SAP S/4HANA, please use the Journal Entry Profiles starting with ‘S4’.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>Once the filters are selected, click ‘Apply Filters’.</p>
<p><img src="media/image6.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:3.27639in" /></p>
<p>If there is a new lease added with a start date from Jan 2019, there will be recurring entries posted from Jan 2019 up to the current month close.</p>
<p><img src="media/image7.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:3.47639in" /></p>
<p><img src="media/image8.png" style="width:6.54306in;height:3.18819in" /></p>
<p>Each blue column header can also be used as an additional filter. These filters can be used to narrow down the lease population to a more granular list by specifying the System Lease IDs, asset or liability amounts above or below a certain threshold, etc. This can help if certain leases need to be approved/exported as opposed to the entire population. Select the dropdown arrow of the appropriate column to ensure all journal entries to be approved are sent to Excel and journal entries preview data is exported to Excel prior to approving.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Select the check box next to each line item you would like to approve. If you would like to check all line items, select the check box next to the column headers to do so.</p></li>
<li><p>Once the desired leases are selected, click ‘Approve Journal Entries’. All the selected leases are now approved and ready to be exported</p></li>
</ul>
<p>The JE Status field on the line items of the corresponding accounting schedules will update to Approved.</p>
<p><img src="media/image9.png" style="width:6.51042in;height:3.40625in" /></p></td>

<tr>
<td colspan="7" style="text-align: left;"><p>The process to export journal entries differs based on the following three groupings:</p>
<ul>
<li><p>AstraZeneca (ECC) - AstraZeneca portfolio leases to be exported following the ‘old’ ECC journal entry processing via Blackline. Thus, these leases have not yet cutover to SAP S/4HANA.</p></li>
<li><p>AstraZeneca (SAP S/4HANA) - AstraZeneca portfolio leases to be exported via the new SAP S/4HANA flat file integration.</p></li>
<li><p>Alexion – Alexion portfolio leases (see similar process to the AstraZeneca SAP S/4HANA process below).</p></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><u>For AstraZeneca (ECC):</u></strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>In the Portfolio module, select ‘Journal Entries to Export (new)’ under Financials and Accounting Links. If you are already in the Journal Entry Approval screen, you can also select the required field in the top left-hand corner and click JE to Export (new).</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image10.png" style="width:6.57778in;height:2.69583in" /></p>
<ol start="2" type="1">
<li><p>This redirects the user to the Journal Entry Export screen. Select the appropriate portfolio (AstraZeneca).</p></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><p>Period – Select the required month.</p></li>
<li><p>Classification Type - IFRS 16.</p></li>
<li><p>Amortization Profile - Select the required profile.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile - Select the required profile.</p></li>
<li><p>Country: Select the required country.</p></li>
<li><p>Currency: Select the required currency.</p></li>
<li><p>Hierarchy - Select the required hierarchy.</p></li>
<li><p>Workflow Status - Reviewed.</p></li>
<li><p>Is Balanced – Yes.</p></li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p>Apply additional filters if desired.</p>
</blockquote>
<ol start="3" type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Apply Filters’. Only journal entry lines for leases that have been approved will appear in the list.</p></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image11.png" style="width:6.57778in;height:2.69583in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>Select ‘Download’ to create an Excel worksheet with the journal entries lines for leases that met the filtered criteria.</p></li>
<li><p>After downloading the Excel file, refer to the below section that outlines the specific country. List of countries who can export only:</p></li>
</ol>
<ul>
<li><p>Ukraine (UA10)</p></li>
<li><p>Russia (RU10, RU30)</p></li>
<li><p>Dutch Holding (Non-SAP NL20)</p></li>
<li><p>Uruguay (Non-SAP UY10)</p></li>
<li><p>Dunkirk (Non-SAP Z007)</p></li>
</ul>
<p>All other countries (that are still following the ECC process and not SAP S/4HANA) other than the above use ‘Export and send to FTP’ function.</p>
<p>This process ensures the journal entries cannot be processed multiple times for the same period.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The user can navigate back to the lease(s) that have completed journal entry processing for the period. All the periods that were approved and exported have a JE Status of ‘Exported’</p>
<p><img src="media/image12.png" style="width:6.55208in;height:3.375in" /><br />
<strong>For AstraZeneca (</strong>SAP S/4HANA<strong>):</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><p>Navigate to the Reports module.</p></li>
<li><p>Search and run “AstraZeneca JE Export”.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the appropriate portfolio (AstraZeneca) and other relevant filters.</p>
<ul>
<li><p>Period – Select the required month.</p></li>
<li><p>Classification Type - IFRS 16.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile/s - Select profiles starting with ‘S4’.</p></li>
<li><p>Currency – Select relevant currency.</p>
<ul>
<li><p><strong>Note</strong>: SAP S/4HANA can only receive extracts with one currency. Thus, please ensure only one currency has been selected for entities with multiple currencies, to avoid downstream errors. (Multiple currencies will result in multiple headers in the JE extract).</p></li>
</ul></li>
<li><p>Workflow Status - Reviewed.</p></li>
<li><p>Country: Select country as required, depending on which country has cutover to SAP S/4HANA.</p></li>
<li><p>Export/Send to SFTP? - Yes</p></li>
<li><p>Select which format you would like the report returned in – Microsoft Excel XLS</p></li>
</ul></li>
</ul>
<p><img src="media/image13.png" style="width:6.55208in;height:5.38542in" /></p>
<ul>
<li><p>Select “Next &gt;&gt;”.</p></li>
</ul>
<p>This process ensures the journal entries cannot be processed multiple times for the same period.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The user can navigate back to the lease(s) that have completed journal entry processing for the period. All the periods that were approved and exported have a JE Status of ‘Exported’.</p>
<p><strong><u>For Alexion:</u></strong></p>
<ol type="1">
<li><p>Navigate to the Reports module.</p></li>
<li><p>Search and run “Alexion JE Export”.</p></li>
<li><p>Select the appropriate portfolio (Alexion) and other relevant filters.</p>
<ol type="a">
<li><p>Period – Select the required month.</p></li>
<li><p>Classification Type - IFRS 16.</p></li>
<li><p>Journal Entry Profile/s</p></li>
<li><p>Workflow Status - Reviewed.</p></li>
<li><p>Country: Select country as required.</p></li>
<li><p>Export/Send to SFTP? - Yes</p></li>
<li><p>Select which format you would like the report returned in – Microsoft Excel XLS</p></li>
</ol></li>
</ol>
<p><img src="media/image14.png" style="width:6.55208in;height:5.13542in" /></p>
<ol start="4" type="1">
<li><p>Next &gt;&gt;”.</p></li>
</ol>
<p>This process ensures the journal entries cannot be processed multiple times for the same period.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> The user can navigate back to the lease(s) that have completed journal entry processing for the period. All the periods that were approved and exported have a JE Status of ‘Exported’</p>
<p>Refer to process <strong>8.3.3.18 Prepare lease accounting entries – Blackline</strong> for guidance on the procedure that follows.</p></td>

#

# PURPOSE

The purpose of this SOP is to describe the standard set of activities that take place to transmit data from CoStar Real Estate Manager to BlackLine for both AZ and Alexion. Following this, data is ingested by BlackLine and transformed into SAP journal entries using the Automated Journal Definition (AJD) functionality, according to specific logic developed in the BlackLine Journal Entry module.

# AUDIENCE

This SOP applies to the below audience:

- GFS Global Lease Team

- GFS Business Administration

# SCOPE

The table indicates the scope of the Systems, Regions, Countries and Business Areas that this document relates to. Anything not explicitly included is excluded:

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 35%" />
<col style="width: 64%" />
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>Business Process</td>
<td>Description</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Global</td>
<td><p>This process applies to all leases for AZ and Alexion that meet the criteria of IFRS16 - Leases, as defined by AstraZeneca GFR, with the exception of the leases which have cutover to SAP S/4HANA during the ongoing staged rollouts to the Axial S/4HANA integration, replacing the Blackline journal entry processing process.</p>
<p>Following completion of the staged rollout across all entities to the Axial S/4HANA integration, the Blackline journal entry from CoStar processing only will become redundant. Blackline will still be used for reconciliations and manual adjustment requirements.</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

This is a monthly process, executed as part of the period end close.

## Process Detail

The following step by step instructions explain how to perform the work involved in the process:

<table>
